title: Objective Personality System Research Corpus
scope: Browser-first research and modelling reference. Summaries are paraphrases, not official OPS definitions.
notice: OPS is a typology framework, not a clinically validated diagnostic instrument. Distinguish framework claims, secondary explanations, hypotheses and independently validated evidence.

models.name: Classic 512-type model
models.description: The official FAQ and several long-running community references describe nine binary coins and 512 possible type combinations. The classic public type code commonly combines two modality letters, two savior functions and an animal stack.
models.caveat: Do not assume that every public source uses the same counting convention or the same revision of the checklist.

models.name: Expanded 2,048-configuration claim
models.description: A separate research page describes eleven binary dimensions: nine cognitive coins plus two social dimensions, giving 2,048 configurations. This is represented as a distinct model rather than silently merged into the classic model.
models.caveat: The page itself states that there are zero peer-reviewed papers on OPS. Treat the expanded taxonomy and its empirical claims as claims to investigate, not as settled consensus or an official replacement.

sources.title: Objective Personality — official website
sources.notes: Primary source for the creators' own framing, resources and services. Some learning materials are membership-gated.

sources.title: FAQ — Objective Personality
sources.notes: Describes the creators' independent-operator typing process, nine binary coins, the 512-type space, and their own account of inter-operator agreement. These are claims made by the source, not independent validation.

sources.title: The Beginnings and Origin
sources.notes: Creators' account of the framework's development and their stated rationale for binary dimensions and repeatable typing.

sources.title: OPS Starter Kit
sources.notes: Accessible overview of human-need coins, letters, animals, modalities and the classic 512-type progression. Not the official OPS organisation.

sources.title: The Objective Personality Type Code
sources.notes: Explains the common code layout, function relationships, animal-stack conventions and examples. Treat as a community explanation of a particular version.

sources.title: OPS Type Analyzer
sources.notes: Useful comparative implementation reference for code fields and compatibility warnings. Its existence does not establish scientific validity or official status.

sources.title: Research — Mahakram
sources.notes: Describes an 11-binary-coin, 2,048-configuration model and explicitly notes zero peer-reviewed OPS papers. Store as a separate claim pending verification.

sources.title: Subjective Personality resources
sources.notes: Provides a community glossary, type database and explanatory articles. Individual pages may be dated and should be version-labelled.

dimensions.name: Gather vs Organize
dimensions.description: The community guide frames this contrast as acquiring new information and variety (Oe) versus organising or stabilising known information (Oi).
dimensions.status: framework concept; interpretation varies by source

dimensions.name: Self vs Tribe
dimensions.description: The community guide frames this contrast as prioritising internally owned identity/reasons (Di) versus calibrating decisions around other people or shared group values (De).
dimensions.status: framework concept; not a clinical construct

dimensions.name: Observer vs Decider
dimensions.description: A framework-level distinction concerning whether observer-side information patterns or decider-side evaluation patterns are treated as the more dominant recurring concern. Exact operationalisation depends on the version/checklist.
dimensions.status: framework concept; requires a version-specific operational definition

dimensions.name: Sensing vs Intuition
dimensions.description: Letter distinction used alongside Oe/Oi to describe observer functions. Avoid treating simplified internet descriptions as sufficient typing criteria.

dimensions.name: Thinking vs Feeling
dimensions.description: Letter distinction used alongside Di/De to describe decider functions. These labels refer to the framework's function vocabulary, not a claim that a person lacks the opposite capacity.

dimensions.name: Consume vs Blast
dimensions.description: The framework groups these as information animals: taking in/working through information (Consume) and organising/communicating information outward (Blast), according to the community guide.

dimensions.name: Play vs Sleep
dimensions.description: The framework groups these as energy animals: interactive engagement (Play) and inward processing/restoration (Sleep), according to community explanations.

dimensions.name: Information vs Energy dominance
dimensions.description: A framework-level balance distinction based on the animal stack. The classic community explanation associates missing an energy animal with information dominance and missing an information animal with energy dominance.

dimensions.name: Sensory modality
dimensions.description: A modality dimension concerning the framework's proposed way of holding or moving sensory information. Masculine/feminine are technical labels in this system and should not be conflated with gender identity.

dimensions.name: Extroverted-decider modality
dimensions.description: A modality dimension applied to the extroverted decider function in the common type code. It is not simply a label for whichever decider function is savior.

dimensions.name: Authority vs Utility
dimensions.description: An additional social dimension named in the independent 2,048-configuration model. Its operational definition and status should be verified against primary documentation before being used as a validated rule.

dimensions.name: Reciprocal-link vs Transactional-spec
dimensions.description: An additional social dimension named in the independent 2,048-configuration model. Stored separately from the classic model pending stronger source confirmation.

functions.name: Extraverted Sensing
functions.summary: In the OPS/Jung-derived vocabulary, combines outward gathering with sensing. This is a framework description, not a measured cognitive mechanism.

functions.name: Introverted Sensing
functions.summary: Combines organising/known information with sensing in the framework's function vocabulary.

functions.name: Extraverted Intuition
functions.summary: Combines outward gathering with intuition in the framework's function vocabulary.

functions.name: Introverted Intuition
functions.summary: Combines organising/known information with intuition in the framework's function vocabulary.

functions.name: Extraverted Thinking
functions.summary: Combines tribe/external evaluation with thinking in the framework's function vocabulary.

functions.name: Introverted Thinking
functions.summary: Combines self/internal evaluation with thinking in the framework's function vocabulary.

functions.name: Extraverted Feeling
functions.summary: Combines tribe/external evaluation with feeling in the framework's function vocabulary.

functions.name: Introverted Feeling
functions.summary: Combines self/internal evaluation with feeling in the framework's function vocabulary.

animals.name: Play
animals.summary: Community explanations describe interactive, outward engagement involving observer and decider processes.

animals.name: Sleep
animals.summary: Community explanations describe inward processing and conserving energy.

animals.name: Blast
animals.summary: Community explanations describe organising and communicating information outward.

animals.name: Consume
animals.summary: Community explanations describe taking in and processing information.

rules.name: Keep model versions separate
rules.statement: A type-space size is valid only relative to an explicitly selected model version and its dimension set. Never merge the classic nine-coin description with the expanded eleven-coin claim without documenting the mapping.

rules.name: Function composition
rules.statement: The common community model composes observer functions from Oe/Oi plus S/N, and decider functions from Di/De plus T/F.

rules.name: Animal stack uniqueness
rules.statement: A complete animal stack, when modelled as a permutation, contains each of P, S, B and C exactly once.

rules.name: Classic savior-animal balance
rules.statement: The classic community guide describes the first two savior animals as one energy animal (P/S) and one information animal (B/C). Apply only where the selected type-code convention supports this rule.

rules.name: Conclusions require linked evidence
rules.statement: Every case hypothesis should link to dated observations, context, alternative explanations and counterevidence. A label or self-description alone is not sufficient evidence in the OPS operator model.

rules.name: Confidence is not probability
rules.statement: The workspace's confidence field is a researcher's confidence in a hypothesis, not a calibrated probability that a type is correct.

rules.name: No clinical diagnosis
rules.statement: OPS labels must not be used to diagnose mental-health conditions, infer protected traits, or make high-stakes decisions about a person.

glossary.definition: OPS term for a preferred or over-relied-upon side of a dimension, as described by the framework.
OPS term for the less-preferred or resisted opposite side of a dimension. It is a framework metaphor, not a moral judgement.

A community term for a type pattern where the usual order of observer/decider saviors is reversed relative to a common MBTI-style expectation. Exact meaning should be checked against the selected version.
A compact notation commonly combining modality letters, two savior functions and an animal stack.
The official FAQ describes independent operators separately typing the same subject and then comparing their results.
A secondary clue or consistency test used to compare a proposed type against other observations or type components. It is not proof on its own.
OPS technical label for a proposed way of handling information. The masculine/feminine terms used by the framework should not be interpreted as a statement about a person's gender identity.
The ordered sequence of Play, Sleep, Blast and Consume in a type code; conventions and compatibility need to be tied to a model version.
